distinguishing_features: A porous TiO2 layer infused with PFPE forms a SLIPS coating on the internal heat-exchanger tube walls.
The anti-fouling action is passive low-surface-energy/low-adhesion modification rather than thermal cycling or setpoint duty changes.
The crude/PFPE interface is used to reduce asphaltene wetting and adhesion so normal flow shear can detach deposits.
The intervention is a material/coating modification of the heat-transfer surface rather than a control-system procedure.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to maintain heat-transfer efficiency in crude preheat exchangers by reducing asphaltene deposit accumulation on tube walls during normal operation.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed TiO2/PFPE SLIPS coating is a testable, physically plausible surface treatment that can lower asphaltene adhesion and preserve heat transfer, although long-term durability remains an empirical question.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 3 changes operating temperature to spall deposits, whereas the candidate changes the tube-wall interface chemistry and structure to reduce adhesion, which is not a routine parameter optimization of that art.
